Estimate indicators with correct survey standard errors

Source: R/estimate.R
bdhs_estimate.Rd

Computes indicators from the registry (bdhs_indicator_list()) for one or several BDHS rounds, nationally or by subgroups, using the complex survey design of the data (bdhs_design()): clusters, sampling-error strata and sample weights. Standard errors use Taylor linearisation (proportions, means, all-women ratios) or the DHS jackknife (medians, fertility and mortality rates).

Usage

bdhs_estimate(
  data,
  indicators = NULL,
  by = NULL,
  survey = NULL,
  level = 0.95,
  scale = 100,
  ci_method = c("logit", "wald"),
  design_args = list()
)

Arguments

data

A BDHS recode data frame (from bdhs_read(), bdhs_simulate() or pooled rounds with a survey_id column) with DHS variable names.

indicators

Character vector of indicator ids (see bdhs_indicator_list()). NULL estimates every indicator available for the recode and round.

by

Optional character vector of grouping variables. Labelled variables are shown with their value labels.

survey

Optional survey reference, overriding detection.

level

Confidence level.

scale

Multiplier for proportions (100 gives percentages, as in DHS reports). Means, medians and rates are never rescaled.

ci_method

"logit" (default) computes confidence intervals for proportions on the logit scale (as survey::svyciprop()), which keeps them inside 0-100; "wald" uses estimate +/- t * SE. Means, medians and rates always use Wald intervals.

design_args

A list of further arguments passed to bdhs_design(), e.g. list(strata = "design") or list(weight = "dv").

Value

A tibble of class bdhs_estimate with columns survey_id, indicator, label, the by variables, estimate, se, ci_low, ci_high, n_unweighted (records in the denominator), n_weighted (weighted denominator; for all-women indicators the estimated number of all women) and api_id (DHS Program API indicator id for comparison with bdhs_indicators).

Details

  • Proportions and means are design-based means over the indicator's denominator population (domain estimation, so standard errors account for the full design).

  • Indicators whose denominator is all women (for example child marriage or teenage childbearing) use the ratio estimator \(\sum w y / \sum w \, awfact / 100\), because only ever-married women were interviewed. The all-woman factor matching a single by variable is used (awfactu for urban/rural, awfactr for division, awfacte for education, awfactw for wealth); other groupings use awfactt.

  • Medians (age at first marriage) use the DHS interpolation on completed ages and jackknife standard errors.

  • Rates call bdhs_fertility() and bdhs_mortality().

Singleton strata are handled with options(survey.lonely.psu = "adjust"), set only while the function runs.

See also

bdhs_validate() to compare with the official values.

Examples

kr <- bdhs_simulate(2017, "KR")
bdhs_estimate(kr, c("rh_del_facility", "rh_del_csection"))
#> # BDHS estimates: 2 indicators | BD2017DHS | 95% CI
#> # A tibble: 2 × 10
#>   survey_id indicator       label     estimate    se ci_low ci_high n_unweighted
#>   <chr>     <chr>           <chr>        <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl>   <dbl>        <int>
#> 1 BD2017DHS rh_del_facility Delivery…     54.7  4.24   45.9    63.3          161
#> 2 BD2017DHS rh_del_csection Delivery…     33.7  3.92   26.2    42.2          161
#> # ℹ 2 more variables: n_weighted <dbl>, api_id <chr>
bdhs_estimate(kr, "rh_del_facility", by = "v025")
#> # BDHS estimates: 1 indicator | BD2017DHS | 95% CI
#> # A tibble: 2 × 11
#>   survey_id indicator     label v025  estimate    se ci_low ci_high n_unweighted
#>   <chr>     <chr>         <chr> <fct>    <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl>   <dbl>        <int>
#> 1 BD2017DHS rh_del_facil… Deli… urban     57.5  6.62   43.6    70.3           77
#> 2 BD2017DHS rh_del_facil… Deli… rural     52.5  5.54   41.2    63.6           84
#> # ℹ 2 more variables: n_weighted <dbl>, api_id <chr>

ir <- bdhs_simulate(2017, "IR")
bdhs_estimate(ir, c("fp_cpr_modern", "ms_married_by_18"), by = "v025")
#> # BDHS estimates: 2 indicators | BD2017DHS | 95% CI
#> # A tibble: 4 × 11
#>   survey_id indicator     label v025  estimate    se ci_low ci_high n_unweighted
#>   <chr>     <chr>         <chr> <fct>    <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl>   <dbl>        <int>
#> 1 BD2017DHS fp_cpr_modern Cont… urban     57.9  2.34   53.0    62.7          255
#> 2 BD2017DHS fp_cpr_modern Cont… rural     53.9  3.18   47.3    60.4          258
#> 3 BD2017DHS ms_married_b… Wome… urban     52.0  5.38   41.0    62.9           42
#> 4 BD2017DHS ms_married_b… Wome… rural     46.0  4.18   37.6    54.7           43
#> # ℹ 2 more variables: n_weighted <dbl>, api_id <chr>
